source_contract.statement: Subscription creation is rejected before mutation when the current user cannot read the skill metadata.
Published fan-out uses current metadata-read access; yanked fan-out uses current facts plus the narrow yank-revocation purpose before dispatch.
All skill visibility decisions for this change are made by VisibilityChecker; the batch resolver contains no independent authorization branch.
Private, namespace-only, hidden, removed-member and disabled-user each have explicit subscribe and fan-out assertions, and denial text resolves in English and Chinese.
VisibilityChecker currently owns hidden, latest-version, visibility, namespace-role and SUPER_ADMIN decisions and has eight production call sites.
Account, namespace, normalized platform roles and an explicit access purpose belong in the full-context VisibilityChecker interface while old overloads and eight callers remain compatible.
The new error.skill.subscription.noPermission values use the frozen English and Chinese copy in plan-r1.
Until the maintainer selects a retained-row policy, unsubscribe remains an escape path and isSubscribed remains an own-relationship boolean without metadata.
No migration, prune, historical subscription cleanup, subscription-count repair or /me/subscriptions redesign is included.
No confirmPublish, event producer, event record, workflow or public PR mutation is included.
evidence: upstream #738 already present in base e8cab738

source_contract.statement: A genuine yank notice is not suppressed solely because that same yank cleared latestVersionId; all other current confidentiality and actor-skip rules still apply.
skillhubEventExecutor uses ThreadPoolExecutor.CallerRunsPolicy, so a running saturated executor executes the task synchronously on the submitting thread instead of rejecting it.
NotificationService.create requires a new physical transaction so afterCommit CallerRuns persists a committed row before NotificationDispatcher pushes SSE.
Batch platform-role derivation is owned by RbacService, performs one binding lookup and applies PlatformRoleDefaults to every requested user.
Pending maintainer choice, implementation retains the getSkillDetail-style metadata gate rather than silently adopting the stricter published-content gate.
Pending maintainer choice, implementation retains the candidate behavior that normalized SUPER_ADMIN roles participate in subscriber fan-out; this is not represented as maintainer approval.

invariants.statement: Subscribe and published fan-out use shared current metadata-read access; yanked fan-out uses the separately named revocation-notice purpose.
Missing or non-active accounts are denied before subscription or recipient effects, including disabled SUPER_ADMIN.
Unauthorized private, hidden and stale-member actors reach no subscription mutation and no recipient-visible notification sink.
Denied subscribe performs no row write, counter increment or event; an allowed non-idempotent subscribe performs all three once.
Losing metadata read access never prevents a user from deleting their existing own subscription.
Unsubscribe decrements exactly when an existing row is deleted and is a no-op for an absent row.
isSubscribed preserves the authenticated caller's own relationship boolean and anonymous false behavior pending maintainer choice.
Fan-out uses account, membership and role facts loaded at event handling time, never a subscription-time snapshot.
Each fan-out performs at most one batch lookup per account, namespace-member and platform-role source and no such lookup inside the candidate loop.
Published fan-out skips the publisher and yanked fan-out skips the actor even when the checker grants access.
The eight existing VisibilityChecker call sites retain observable behavior and both old overloads produce a byte-identical base/candidate legacy matrix.
Reflection, generated, external and runtime-conditional surfaces remain explicit audit evidence rather than being treated as absent.
A genuine yank notice is not denied solely by the latestVersionId null state caused by that yank; current hidden, visibility, account, namespace and actor rules remain.
RbacService performs one batch binding lookup and returns a PlatformRoleDefaults-normalized role set for every requested distinct user.
Account, membership, platform-role or namespace authority failure on either fan-out path occurs before every recipient row and SSE sink.
Eligibility filtering and actor removal do not reorder readable candidates through dispatcher, committed Notification rows or SSE notifications.
With executor capacity, the registered subscriber listener runs on the configured async executor only after source commit and produces a committed row before matching SSE.
Source rollback and publication without an active transaction do not invoke eligibility, dispatcher, Notification persistence or SSE.
A running saturated configured executor executes the after-commit subscriber task synchronously on and blocks the publisher thread while preserving the ordinary committed-row then SSE effects.
